issues.display_title: Issue #217: Handle Miss Worker Caused by Unprovisioned Dev Environment
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Fix Viewer JSON Worker Infinite Requeue Loop & Miss Worker Handling

Files Changed

  • src/workers/viewer_json.go
  • src/workers/worker.go
  • src/workers/workers_test.go (new)

Resolution Strategy

  1. Requeue Loop Prevention in Consumer Engine (src/workers/worker.go):

    • Inspect msg.Redelivered. If a message fails after having already been redelivered, discard it using msg.Nack(false, false).
    • Apply a 1-second backoff delay on the first failure (!msg.Redelivered) before requeueing with msg.Nack(false, true) to eliminate high-frequency CPU/DB spinning.

  2. Miss Worker & Record Not Found Handling (src/workers/viewer_json.go):

    • When a job references an exhibition that does not exist in the database (e.g. from a miss worker or deleted record), GORM returns gorm.ErrRecordNotFound.
    • The handler checks errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound). If matched, it logs that the record was not found and returns nil, allowing the message to be acknowledged (Ack) and permanently cleared from the queue.
    • Malformed JSON payloads that fail json.Unmarshal are also skipped (return nil) rather than returned as errors.

  3. Automated Unit Testing (src/workers/workers_test.go):

    • Added unit tests verifying that malformed payloads and empty exhibition IDs are safely acknowledged without returning errors.

Code Changes

1. Consumer Engine Anti-Loop (src/workers/worker.go)

if err := w.Handle(ctx, msg); err != nil {
    log.Printf("❌ Worker %q handle error: %v", queue, err)
    if msg.Redelivered {
        log.Printf("⚠️  Worker %q message already redelivered — discarding to prevent infinite loop", queue)
        _ = msg.Nack(false, false)
    } else {
        time.Sleep(1 * time.Second)
        _ = msg.Nack(false, true)
    }
} else {
    _ = msg.Ack(false)
}

2. Miss Worker & Record Not Found Handling (src/workers/viewer_json.go)

func (w *ViewerJSONWorker) Handle(ctx context.Context, msg amqp.Delivery) error {
    _ = ctx

    var payload queues.ViewerJSONPayload
    if err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Body, &payload); err != nil {
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] unmarshal error: %v — skipping invalid payload", err)
        return nil
    }

    exhibitionID := strings.TrimSpace(payload.ExhibitionID)
    if exhibitionID == "" {
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] missing exhibition_id — skipping")
        return nil
    }

    log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] start exhibition_id=%s", exhibitionID)
    if err := exhibition.WriteViewerJSONFromDiskAndRedis(exhibitionID); err != nil {
        if errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) {
            log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] exhibition_id=%s not found in DB — skipping job", exhibitionID)
            return nil
        }
        log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] failed exhibition_id=%s: %v", exhibitionID, err)
        return err
    }

    log.Printf("[ViewerJSONWorker] done exhibition_id=%s", exhibitionID)
    return nil
}

Behavior and Recovery

  • Automatic Queue Clearance:
    When workers are restarted with the new code, stuck messages caused by miss worker events are consumed once, recognized as record not found, logged, and immediately acknowledged (Ack). The queue drains cleanly without manual purging.
  • Fail-Safe Operation:
    Even if environment variables (RabbitMQ host / queue prefix) are misconfigured or unprovisioned, workers will never enter a high-throughput infinite loop that degrades server performance.

Verification

Unit Tests

go test -v -count=1 ./src/workers/...

Output:

=== RUN   TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_MalformedJSON
2026/09/25 08:07:37 [ViewerJSONWorker] unmarshal error: invalid character 'o' in literal null (expecting 'u') — skipping invalid payload
--- PASS: TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_MalformedJSON (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_EmptyExhibitionID
2026/09/25 08:07:37 [ViewerJSONWorker] missing exhibition_id — skipping
--- PASS: TestViewerJSONWorker_Handle_EmptyExhibitionID (0.00s)
PASS
ok      villume-backend-go/src/workers  0.047s

Build Verification

go build ./cmd/worker-viewer-json

Compiles cleanly with zero errors.

Overview

The background worker service (worker-viewer-json and worker.go) processes asynchronous queue messages for rebuilding viewer.json files for exhibitions. The system experienced a critical issue where workers entered a high-frequency requeue loop (~950+ req/sec) repeatedly failing with record not found and exhausting CPU and database resources.

Problem & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Miss Worker Due to Missing / Unisolated Dev Environment:

    • A dedicated, isolated RabbitMQ environment for Development had not yet been provisioned.
    • Consequently, the Dev server connected to the Live RabbitMQ broker (192.168.1.55) and consumed from the Live queue (villume_live-viewer-json), while remaining connected to the Development database (villume_db_dev on 192.168.1.202).
    • This caused a miss worker condition (cross-environment worker mismatch):
      • Jobs published with Live exhibition IDs were consumed by the Dev worker, or Dev exhibition IDs were queued into the Live queue.
      • When queried against the wrong database, the query returned [rows:0] resulting in gorm.ErrRecordNotFound (record not found).

  2. Severe Infinite Requeue Loop:

    • In src/workers/worker.go, the message consumer loop unconditionally responded to any handler error with: 
      if err := w.Handle(ctx, msg); err != nil {
    log.Printf("❌ Worker %q handle error: %v", queue, err)
    _ = msg.Nack(false, true) // requeue = true
}
    • RabbitMQ immediately pushed the rejected message back to the front of the queue without delay or retry limits.
    • The worker immediately re-consumed the same message, triggering an infinite hot loop of ~950–1000 deliveries per second, saturating database connections, disk I/O, and CPU.

Goals

  1. Eliminate Requeue Loops Completely:

    • Prevent any message from looping infinitely upon failure.
    • Guard against repeated redeliveries (msg.Redelivered) by rejecting failed messages without requeue (requeue = false), cleanly removing them from the queue.
    • Add backoff delay on initial retry attempts to suppress CPU/DB traffic spikes during transient issues.

  2. Resilient Worker Handling for Miss Worker Scenarios:

    • Provide worker-level resilience even if environment isolation has not yet been fully configured or if a miss worker event occurs.
    • For permanent errors like record not found (gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) in ViewerJSONWorker, log the event and acknowledge (Ack) the message to drop it without requeueing.
    • Silently skip malformed or corrupted JSON payloads in workers instead of returning errors to the requeue loop.

Scope

  • src/workers/viewer_json.go: Handle record not found and unmarshal errors as non-requeueable jobs.
  • src/workers/worker.go: Implement redelivery guards and backoff in the consumer loop to prevent infinite requeuing.
  • src/workers/email.go: Safely skip unmarshal errors without triggering requeue.
  • src/workers/workers_test.go: Automated unit tests verifying worker error and payload handling.

Implementation

issues.display_title: Issue #218: Email Queue Environment Prefix Isolation
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Email Queue Environment Prefix Isolation

Files Changed

  • src/lib/queues/mail.go (new)
  • src/lib/queues/mail_test.go (new)
  • src/workers/email.go
  • src/workers/workers_test.go
  • src/action/v1/auth/forgotPassword.go
  • src/action/v1/auth/authGoogle.go
  • src/action/v1/auth/registerUser.go
  • src/action/v1/auth/resendOtp.go
  • src/action/v1/billing/coupon/createCoupon.go
  • src/action/v1/billing/successCheckout.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/createPendingPayment.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/createUnpaidPayment.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/remindCreateExhibition.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/remindCreditCardExpired.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/remindOneDayExpiredSubscription.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/remindThreeDaysExpiredSubscription.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/renewalSubscription.go
  • src/action/v1/cron/subscriptionHasExpired.go
  • src/action/v1/support/contactUs.go
  • src/controllers/dev/devController.go

Resolution Strategy

  1. Dynamic Queue Resolver (src/lib/queues/mail.go):
    • Implemented queues.MailQueue() reading PREFIX_RABBITMQ (or prefix_rabbitmq):
      • PREFIX_RABBITMQ=villume_live -> villume_live-mail
      • PREFIX_RABBITMQ=villume_dev -> villume_dev-mail
      • Unset / empty -> villume-mail
  2. Worker Migration (src/workers/email.go):
    • Updated w.Queue() to return queues.MailQueue().
    • Updated w.Handle() to return nil upon json.Unmarshal failure, dropping malformed payloads immediately without requeueing.
  3. Publisher Migration:
    • Replaced all 16 hardcoded "villume-mail" string literals across all application endpoints with queues.MailQueue().
  4. Automated Testing (src/lib/queues/mail_test.go):
    • Added unit test covering fallback when unset, villume_live prefix, and villume_dev prefix.

Code Changes

1. Dynamic Email Queue Resolver (src/lib/queues/mail.go)

package queues

// MailQueue returns the RabbitMQ queue for asynchronous email sending jobs.
// When PREFIX_RABBITMQ is set (e.g. villume_live), the queue is "{prefix}-mail".
func MailQueue() string {
    if p := rabbitMQPrefix(); p != "" {
        return p + "-mail"
    }
    return "villume-mail"
}

2. Email Worker (src/workers/email.go)

func (w *EmailWorker) Queue() string { return queues.MailQueue() }

func (w *EmailWorker) Handle(ctx context.Context, msg amqp.Delivery) error {
    var payload EmailPayload
    if err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Body, &payload); err != nil {
        log.Printf("[EmailWorker] failed to unmarshal: %v — skipping malformed payload", err)
        return nil
    }
    // ...
}

3. Updated Publisher Example (src/action/v1/auth/forgotPassword.go)

_ = rabbitmq.Publish(c.Context(), queues.MailQueue(), emailPayload)

Behavior and Recovery

  • Full Queue Separation:
    • Live publishes to and consumes from villume_live-mail.
    • Dev publishes to and consumes from villume_dev-mail.
    • Workers from different environments no longer cross-consume email jobs, eliminating foreign key violation errors on mail_histories.
  • Zero Downtime Migration:
    • Existing live workers running without PREFIX_RABBITMQ continue using villume-mail. Once PREFIX_RABBITMQ is configured, both producer and consumer switch synchronously to {prefix}-mail.

Verification

Unit Tests

go test -v -count=1 ./src/lib/queues/...
go test -v -count=1 ./src/workers/...

Output:

=== RUN   TestMailQueue
--- PASS: TestMailQueue (0.00s)
PASS
ok      villume-backend-go/src/lib/queues   0.054s

=== RUN   TestEmailWorker_Handle_MalformedJSON
--- PASS: TestEmailWorker_Handle_MalformedJSON (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestEmailWorker_Handle_MissingRecipient
--- PASS: TestEmailWorker_Handle_MissingRecipient (0.00s)
PASS
ok      villume-backend-go/src/workers  0.047s

Build Verification

go build ./cmd/api
go build ./cmd/worker-email

All binaries compile cleanly with zero errors.

Overview

The worker-email service processes asynchronous transactional email jobs (registration, OTP, password reset, billing receipts, subscription reminders, and contact forms). Previously, the queue name was hardcoded as "villume-mail" across EmailWorker and all 16 publishing endpoints in the codebase.

Problem & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Cross-Environment Queue Collision:

    • Because "villume-mail" was hardcoded without environment prefixing (unlike ViewerJSONQueue()), Development and Live environments connected to the same RabbitMQ broker contended for the identical queue.
    • Live transactional emails were picked up by Dev workers, and Dev test emails were picked up by Live workers.

  2. Foreign Key Constraint Violations on mail_histories:

    • When EmailWorker completes sending an email, it logs the event into mail_histories referencing UserID (which has a foreign key constraint to users(id)).
    • If a Dev worker consumed a Live email job, the UserID did not exist in the Dev database, causing database foreign key violations ([EmailWorker] failed to insert history: ...). As a result, email audit history in the Live database was lost.

  3. Malformed Payload Handling:

    • EmailWorker previously returned errors when json.Unmarshal failed, causing unnecessary requeueing of permanently malformed payloads.

Goals

  1. Namespace Email Queues by Environment (PREFIX_RABBITMQ):
    • Implement queues.MailQueue() mirroring the ViewerJSONQueue() pattern:
      • villume_live-mail when PREFIX_RABBITMQ=villume_live
      • villume_dev-mail when PREFIX_RABBITMQ=villume_dev
      • Fallback to villume-mail when the variable is unset.
  2. Migrate All Email Publishers:
    • Replace all hardcoded "villume-mail" occurrences with queues.MailQueue() across auth, billing, cron, support, and dev controllers.
  3. Gracefully Skip Malformed Payloads:
    • Log and skip (return nil) malformed JSON payloads in EmailWorker to drop unparseable messages immediately.
  4. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Add unit tests verifying prefix resolution and malformed payload skipping.

Scope

  • src/lib/queues/mail.go: Helper resolving dynamic email queue name from PREFIX_RABBITMQ.
  • src/lib/queues/mail_test.go: Unit tests for MailQueue().
  • src/workers/email.go: Use queues.MailQueue() and skip unmarshal errors.
  • src/action/v1/auth/*: Update forgotPassword.go, authGoogle.go, registerUser.go, resendOtp.go.
  • src/action/v1/billing/*: Update coupon/createCoupon.go, successCheckout.go.
  • src/action/v1/cron/*: Update all 8 cron handlers publishing email jobs.
  • src/action/v1/support/contactUs.go: Update contact form email publishers.
  • src/controllers/dev/devController.go: Update test email publisher.

Implementation
